title: Introduce policy index and KMS provenance adapter
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: compliance teams requested better observability and deterministic decisioning for RBAC v2 evaluations when KMS-bound resources are used. The current policy decision path does extra lookups to resolve KMS provenance which increases tail latency and makes post-hoc audit correlation expensive. This PR adds two small, tightly-scoped components: (1) a policy-index service that maintains compact fingerprints and quick-match indices for RBAC v2 policy templates and (2) a KMS provenance adapter that attaches canonical KMS usage metadata to the audit envelope and exposes a provenance lookup API used by the policy index. Motivation: reduce per-decision latency, make audit logs richer and machine-friendly, and enable safe incremental rollout of residency-sensitive KMS checks. Changes: - New service: internal/policyindex: stores policy fingerprints, matching rules, and a lightweight cache with TTLs; exposes /v1/match and /v1/refresh endpoints. - KMS adapter: internal/kms/provenance: extracts KMS key origin, provider, region-assertion and returns a provenance token included in Authorization-Audit headers. - Audit envelope enrichment: audit/encoder now includes kms_provenance.token and provenance_fingerprint fields; audit forwarder accepts provenance tokens and stores them in the canonical audit index. - Policy decision path: authz/engine calls policy-index/match first; if no match falls back to full policy evaluation. Feature flag: rollout.policy_index=true gates behavior. Backwards compatibility: when the feature flag is disabled, system behavior is unchanged. When enabled, the fallback path guarantees identical decisions. Testing and validation: unit + integration tests added (authz engine, policy-index, audit pipeline). Load test harness shows p95 decision latency reduced by ~0.8ms on our benchmark workload with 10% policy cache hit rate; no regressions on throughput. Security review: key materials are never persisted in the index; provenance tokens are short-lived and signed with the platform KMS. Migration and rollout notes: - Step 0: deploy policy-index in shadow mode (feature flag off) for 24h and collect match metrics. - Step 1: enable rollout.policy_index=shadow to populate index and verify audit correlations. - Step 2: toggle rollout.policy_index=true for 10% of traffic and monitor decision parity alerts. - Step 3: increase rollout to 100% after 72h with no parity errors. Monitoring: new dashboards added: AuthZ / decision parity, PolicyIndex hit-rate, KMS provenance errors. Alerts: parity-drop >0.1% for 30m escalates to SEC-ONCALL. Checklist: - [x] Security review completed (SEC-77) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests with audit forwarder - [x] Load benchmark run - [x] Documentation: README for policy-index and ops runbook - [x] Feature flag gating added Notes: This PR touches only internal APIs and the audit envelope schema; migration is non-breaking because fields are additive and the policy-index is optional. Follow-up work: garbage-collection of old provenance tokens (ENG-4202), extend index to support conditional attributes (ENG-4210).

review_comments: Ethan Rivera: can the policy-index fingerprint collide with templated policies? please include the algorithm rationale. -> reply (Maya Chen): fingerprint uses a canonicalized AST + HMAC with per-deployment salt to avoid accidental collision; doc string added to proto and tests cover near-collisions.

Samira Patel: audit schema change looks additive, but ensure downstream sinks ignore unknown fields. Suggest adding a schema version header. -> reply (Maya Chen): added Audit-Schema-Version header and compatibility tests to forwarder; forwarder now logs and drops unknown fields safely.

Luca Moretti: load test numbers look promising; what about worst-case where provenance service is down? -> reply (Maya Chen): policy-index match has a strict 50ms local timeout and falls back to full policy evaluation; added circuit-breaker metrics and a unit test that simulates gateway failures.
Ethan Rivera: security team should confirm token lifetime is safe. -> reply (Samira Patel): SEC reviewed and approved token lifetime 5m (SEC-77).
release_notes: Add a non-breaking policy index for faster RBACv2 decisioning and a KMS provenance adapter that enriches audit envelopes with signed provenance tokens. Rollout is feature-flagged; see ops runbook for staged rollout steps.
